title: Anonymous browsing: complete old and new pages across cutover
banner: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Load old/new page assets during cutover; successful HTML alone must not pass rendering.

sourceContract.readme: Anonymous browsing: Render a complete page while deployments change, including assets referenced before cutover.
sourceContract.backlog: Add a browsing journey that loads old/new pages and assets during migration.
sourceContract.acceptance: Complete rendered-page correctness is verified, not merely successful HTML status.
sourceContract.portableCard: Load old/new page assets during cutover; successful HTML alone must not pass rendering.
sourceContract.nativeSibling: Conduct one browsing transition; verify complete rendered-page and required-asset correctness.

preconditions: All version, HTTP-status, asset, cache, route, render, readiness, anonymous-context, timing and journey observations are fixed fictional teaching DATA ONLY.
Old v1 HTML is captured before fictional cutover and its required CSS/script/image references remain v1 after cutover.
A new anonymous page starts after fictional cutover and requires complete v2 HTML/CSS/script/image correctness.
Typed original budget is a whole integer 100 through 5000 fictional ms, declared before starting; default 2000.
Fixed old/new journey durations are 420/360 ms; the slow new-page fixture uses 2400 ms. These are not measured latency.
Known true readiness admits cutover; failed or unknown readiness denies exposure without inventing success.
Owned local fixture files illustrate actual browser rendering only; no actual HTTP transport, SWA or Azure behavior is claimed.
actions: Choose one of eleven fixed conditions and confirm literal DATA ONLY.
Capture old HTML, optionally verify insufficient evidence, check readiness and record admitted nominal cutover.
Load old required references after cutover, then load and render the new page.
Verify each complete rendered page, required asset/status/version/cache receipt, route, anonymous context, journey and original budget.
Compare known missing assets, cached wrong version, semantic rendering defects, lost browsing context, slow HTML 200 and unknown receipts.
Reset with the keyboard while preserving the complete bounded in-page history.
assertions: HTML 200 alone and a nominal cutover cannot pass complete-page verification.
Both version-correct required-asset and rendered-page checks must pass along with readiness, observed routing, anonymous context and original journey budgets.
A required failure dominates concurrent missing evidence; failed started journeys stay in the denominator.
Required asset/version/cache/render/readiness/route/context/journey unknowns remain unverified, never inferred from HTML success.
Positive local fixture rendering does not erase a fixed journey failure or unknown route.
The actual local browser observes old/new CSS, script output and image dimensions, missing-resource failures and semantic render defects.
Exact typed inputs, literal consent, immutable issued states, bounded sessions and ordered steps reject coercion, forged receipts and repeated actions.
Six runs and three advancing verifications per run are retained without pruning; resets restore defaults and archive failures.
Reset during a pending local asset load records unknown local proof and cannot apply stale render success.
Actual keyboard/error/reset/missing-model UX and CSP inline/eval/local-connection denials are tested.

verification.iac: N/A after genuine RED: resource-free local lesson; no infrastructure generated.

limits: No actual SWA, cloud, registry, resource, asset deployment, cache, route, readiness, user session, user journey or cutover operation.
No external URLs or application framework; all rendering illustrations are owned local fixture assets.
No native Azure proof, source-parent completion, production Node.js 24 validation, five-nines result or SLA.
Anonymous context means fixed navigation continuity only; no authentication or actual session implementation.
Reset retains in-page history; deliberate reload starts a new session, not durable backend persistence.
The published browser helper has known page/context/cleanup lifecycle limitations; its inactive recovery prototype remains unqualified.
B-S131 and D-S131 require separately approved native prerequisites and original acceptance observations.
Parent alone accepts this one original frozen S unit once; testing, repair, proof and refinement earn zero extra credits.
Active catalog-owned C005-C008/local-harness and all root/shared/source/ledger files are untouched by implementation.
